_comment: The partitioned 30 Hz chain with BOTH clusters taken whole: yolo occupies all four P cores per frame (machine_width 4 on CPU_P, which is also what makes it IME-eligible -- smt.vmadot is legal only on cluster 0), and nav occupies all four E cores per dispatch with control sharing that cluster. nav and control are consecutive links of one chain, so for a given frame they are not resident at once. gen_root is gen_mb_shard_nav: gen_mb_shard profiles fused_full at topo_0 only, and a width the profile does not carry is costed as one hart, so a wider nav could never shorten anything. That tree adds fused_full's measured topo_0_1 and topo_0_1_2_3 tables from the standalone harness (scripts/emit_shard_profile.py --net fused_full --runs-dir .../nav_standalone; 3.91 / 3.64 / 3.54 ms over its 15 dispatches at widths 1 / 2 / 4). mlp_control stays width 1: it is profiled at topo_0 only.

chain.deadline_rationale: a frame's goal reaches control within its nav window (77.8 ms); control is phase-locked at 100 Hz and acts on the newest goal
